judged_text: For COLLECTIVE team events, team member destination calendars are only pushed when evt.destinationCalendar is already non-null, and the booking row only connects destinationCalendar[0]. When neither the eventType nor the organizer has a destination calendar but team members do (evt.destinationCalendar is null), the push is silently skipped by optional chaining and collective bookings create no calendar events for members who configured calendars — the PR's stated intent (collective multiple-host destination calendars) silently does not apply in that case, without any accepted decision to exclude it.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Later, for COLLECTIVE team events, member calendars are appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` which is a no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. Since `teamDestinationCalendars` is populated from other users’ `user.destinationCalendar`, this means member destination calendars are silently dropped in exactly the scenario described. Downstream, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` only iterates destinations when `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`, so those member events won’t be created. Additionally, the booking create only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0]`, further showing only the first destination is persisted/used (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`).
